intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Three oil tankers hit mines in Hormuz
items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said late on Monday that three oil tankers had struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Two of the ships hit mines in the eastern part of the strait, and fires broke out on all three vessels. The Guard said US air cover had failed to prevent the incidents. It promised to release video of the blasts and warned ships against using "unauthorized routes". Iran announced on 12 July that it had closed the strait after US strikes resumed.

gloss.strait: a narrow area of sea between two pieces of land
gloss.mine: a hidden bomb that explodes when a ship touches it
gloss.break out: to start suddenly, usually a fire or a fight

items.title: Allies warn of Russian nuclear weapon in space
items.text: Western intelligence services have warned that Russia could launch a satellite carrying a nuclear warhead as early as December. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed the reports on Monday. A nuclear weapon in orbit would break the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which Russia has signed. The US Defence Intelligence Agency has said such a weapon could damage or destroy thousands of satellites, including those used for telecoms and traffic control.

gloss.warhead: the explosive part of a missile or bomb
gloss.dismiss: to say that something is not worth considering
gloss.orbit: the path of an object moving around the Earth
gloss.treaty: a formal written agreement between countries
gloss.satellite: a machine sent into space to circle the Earth

items.title: Burnham rules out rejoining EU without vote
items.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told Parliament on Monday that rejoining the EU without another referendum would be "unthinkable". He said he personally favours renewed membership, but that the government has no fixed position. Ministers will set out options for closer ties with Europe next month. Mr Burnham has ruled out rejoining the single market or the customs union in this Parliament. Four former Conservative prime ministers have warned against reopening the Brexit debate.

gloss.referendum: a vote by all the people on one important question
gloss.unthinkable: too extreme or unlikely to be considered
gloss.set out: to explain or present something clearly
gloss.customs union: a group of countries that charge the same taxes on imported goods
gloss.rule out: to say that something will not happen or is not possible

items.title: UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup
items.text: FIFA has awarded the 2035 Women's World Cup to the United Kingdom. The decision was made at a virtual extraordinary congress, and the bid was approved without opposition. The 2031 tournament will go to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica. That edition will be the first to feature 48 teams, up from 32. The number of matches will rise from 64 to 104.

gloss.award: to officially give something to someone
gloss.bid: a formal offer to host or do something
gloss.congress: a formal meeting of members of an organisation
gloss.edition: one version of a regular event

items.title: LaLiga says fan data stolen in cyberattack
items.text: The Spanish football league LaLiga has said that a cyberattack on one of its fan platforms exposed personal data. The attack took place between 14 and 16 November. LaLiga said an unauthorised person had stolen information belonging to fans registered with its digital services and with some clubs. Security teams contained the attack on 16 November. The league has not said how many people were affected.

gloss.cyberattack: an attempt to damage or steal from computer systems
gloss.expose: to make something private visible to others
gloss.register: to put your name on an official list

items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
items.text: Nvidia's board has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director, with immediate effect. The vote was unanimous. The company praised Mr Huang's "candor and ability to lead". It said the board had spoken to senior US government officials, who helped persuade it that his return "poses no national security risk". The decision has caused a lot of discussion in Washington.

gloss.reinstate: to give someone their old job or position back
gloss.board: the group of people who run a company

items.title: Ten-thousand-year-old artefacts go on show in Ankara
items.text: Thirty-four prehistoric artefacts from four sites in Şanlıurfa were displayed at the Presidential National Library in Ankara from 17 to 23 November. The sites are Göbeklitepe, Karahantepe, Sefertepe and Sayburç. The objects come from the Stone Hills Project and date from the Pre-Pottery Neolithic period, about 10,000 to 7,000 BC. Göbeklitepe is among the oldest known monumental sites in the world.

gloss.artefact: an old object made by people, often found by archaeologists
gloss.prehistoric: from the time before written history
gloss.date from: to have existed since a certain time
gloss.site: a place where something important happened or was found

items.title: Australian music legend Molly Meldrum dies at 83
items.text: Ian "Molly" Meldrum, the Australian music journalist and television presenter, died on Monday morning at Epworth Hospital in Melbourne after a long illness. He was 83. Victoria's premier, Ben Carroll, said the family had accepted an offer of a state funeral. The date and place have not yet been announced. Meldrum was famous for his cowboy hat and for the pop show Countdown, which ran on ABC from 1974 to 1987.

gloss.journalist: a person who writes or reports the news
gloss.presenter: a person who introduces a TV or radio programme
gloss.state funeral: a public funeral paid for by the government
gloss.long illness: a sickness lasting a long time
gloss.pass away: a polite way to say someone has died

items.title: Trump says China may buy 250 more Boeings
items.text: President Donald Trump has said China may buy another 250 Boeing aircraft. Speaking to CNBC, he said he had "sold 250 Boeings to China, and I think they're going to do another 250". Such an order could expand an earlier agreement between the two countries. Boeing is one of the biggest US exporters. The company has not yet commented on the president's remarks.

gloss.aircraft: a plane or other flying machine
gloss.exporter: a company or country that sells goods abroad
gloss.order: a request to make and supply goods

items.title: GTA VI is the biggest launch in PlayStation history
items.text: Sony says Grand Theft Auto VI was the biggest game launch in PlayStation history. More than 39 million players tried it on PS5 between 19 and 22 November. They played 683 million hours in total, an average of 17.4 hours each. Sony also said GTA VI was the first game played on 70 per cent of new PS5 consoles. The figures come from Sony's own internal data. Rockstar released its first free update on 23 November.

gloss.launch: the time when a new product first goes on sale
gloss.unique: counted only once, even if repeated
gloss.cumulative: added up over a period of time
gloss.update: a new version of software that fixes problems
